note: Ranges and default values for the controls, with the basis for each default. A default of null means the value comes from the country's data file. Values are fractions: 0.02 means 2%. Defaults marked illustrative are starting values for exploring scenarios, not estimates.

growth.basis: Country baseline: the average of the IMF's projections for the five years after the starting year.

primaryBalance.basis: The latest full-year value in the country's data.

capLevel.basis: Used only when the cap is fixed. Starts at the country's current yield.

passThrough.basis: Illustrative assumption until the historical presets are computed from data. The default will then be the lowest preset.

baselineInflation.basis: The country's average inflation since 1972, as historical precedent: the years since the United States ended the dollar's convertibility into gold in August 1971.

runoff.basis: Illustrative assumption: the central bank keeps its holdings steady as a share of GDP.

yieldResponse.basis: Illustrative assumption: about 3 basis points of yield for each point of GDP of debt, one value for all four countries. To be confirmed against Laubach (2009) and Gamber and Seliski (2019) before publishing.

maturity.basis: The average maturity of the country's debt, from its data file.

priceSensitive.note: A group's default comes from the country's data file where the data separates holders by type. Otherwise it is the illustrative value here.

foreign.basis: Illustrative assumption for countries whose data cannot separate foreign official from foreign private holders.

passThroughPresets.label: Pandemic
passThroughPresets.episode: United States and United Kingdom, 2020 to 2022
